Looks fun but doesn't fully work with multiplayer, and this game is pretty dependent on multiplayer as a friend game. The controls are server-sided, meaning all your inputs are ran through the server and delivered back to you. If the controls and physics were client-sided then multiplayer would be playable. The reason some people find multiplayer to work just fine is because them and all their friends were on low ping (like fiber optic) but for people like me who don't have the greatest of internet (like DSL, mobile service, etc) it's like I'm playing from the cloud with 300MS of input lag. Again, this game looks pretty fun, but there are some major issues with multiplayer.

As a guy who played this game a few years back on Xbox, the game's grabbing mechanics have been completely ruined by "quality of life" updates. If the grabbing assist radius was consistently far, that would be one thing, but the priority system is so convoluted it borders on unplayable. It would have been so easy to just make the hands point in the direction of the camera and grab onto the nearest object within a small radius. You could absolutely prioritize vehicle controls, handles, and packages, but the current system seems to prioritize the object nearest the camera position rather than the one nearest your hands. The effect of this is a system that attempts to grab onto objects far behind you instead of the one directly in front of you. The most obvious and testable example of this is any mission with a helicopter involved. When you put the package in the back or even on a hook and try to grab the controls, the game points your hands behind you to try to grab onto the package. The problem is so apparent that most helicopter missions become impossible when playing alone and all other missions become unplayably frustrating.
